one_liner: GNU's plain-C LP/MIP solver with MathProg modelling; ranks ahead of lp_solve but far behind HiGHS and Clp.
what_it_does: GLPK is a callable C library (glpk.h: glp_create_prob, glp_load_matrix, glp_simplex, glp_exact, glp_interior, glp_intopt) plus the glpsol command-line solver for linear and mixed-integer programs. It reads MPS, CPLEX LP and GNU MathProg (an AMPL subset) models, so it doubles as a small modelling system. Its API is its own; it is not a drop-in for lp_solve's lprec interface.
how_it_is_fast: Revised primal and dual simplex with projected steepest-edge pricing, Harris' two-pass ratio test and an optional long-step (bound-flipping) dual ratio test (GLP_RT_FLIP), on an LU basis factorization with Forrest-Tomlin or Schur-complement updates (bflib). An LP presolver, a primal-dual interior-point method with AMD ordering, and a branch-and-cut MIP solver with Gomory, MIR, cover and clique cuts plus feasibility-pump and proximity heuristics complete it. The edge over lp_solve comes from these standard techniques; there is no parallelism or SIMD.
when_to_use: You use lp_solve or need a free embeddable LP/MIP solver, and GPL-3.0 linking is acceptable: GLPK beat lp_solve in every third-party table seen (about 3.8-4.3x on Mittelmann-derived 2019 tables, about 1.5x on ALGLIB's NETLIB set).
Small to medium LPs and easy MIPs where solve time is not the bottleneck and a dependency-free C library is worth more than top speed.
Models written in GNU MathProg or AMPL-like syntax that you want to solve from the glpsol CLI without a commercial modelling system.
You need an exact rational-arithmetic simplex (glp_exact, with GMP) to certify an optimal basis.
Browser or Node use through the Emscripten build (glpk.js) or a vendored source tree (igraph ships GLPK 5.0 in vendor/glpk).
when_not_to_use: LP speed matters: GLPK sits about 5x behind HiGHS and about 20-26x behind Clp on the same 2019 tables, and Mittelmann's current LPopt benchmark (29 Apr 2026: COPT 1.00, HiGHS 13.07, CLP 27.38) no longer includes GLPK at all.
Hard MIPs or large instances that need multithreading: the solver runs single-threaded and was reported (Sandia 2013, snippet only) unable to match Clp or CPLEX.
Proprietary or permissively licensed products: GPL-3.0-or-later, so linking makes the combined work GPL.
Large LPs through the interior-point path: glp_interior is a basic primal-dual method, and in 5.0 the QMD ordering is a stub that aborts.
You need an actively developed project: 5.0 (Dec 2020) is still the release every packager ships, there is no public repository, and GCC 15 needs a downstream patch.

integration.form: static lib | shared lib (autotools build of the GNU tarball); also a source-drop (igraph vendors src/ with its own CMake)
integration.dependencies: none required; optional GMP (exact simplex; Homebrew and conda-forge build --with-gmp), zlib, libltdl/dlfcn, ODBC and MySQL drivers for MathProg tables; bundles copies of SuiteSparse AMD/COLAMD and MiniSat (Debian and msys2 patch these out)
integration.min_toolchain: ANSI C compiler; GCC 15's default C23 mode breaks on minisat.h's 'typedef int bool' unless patched (msys2 0005-fix-build-with-gcc-15.patch, igraph's own fix)
integration.platforms: any: POSIX autotools, Windows (w32/w64 MSVC build files, mingw-w64 via msys2), every Julia Yggdrasil target, WebAssembly via Emscripten (glpk.js)
integration.thread_safety: The global environment pointer (env/tls.c) is thread-local only if the TLS macro is defined at build time; then independent problems can be solved in separate threads, one glp_prob per thread. The 4.60 autotools config.h.in defines no TLS; whether 5.0's configure enables it by default was not checked (configure.ac for 5.0 was unreachable).
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — not API-compatible with lp_solve (glp_prob/glp_simplex vs lprec); models move between them through files such as MPS, or the model-building code is rewritten

gotchas: Any detected error, including an invalid control parameter, prints a message and calls abort() (env/error.c); only a glp_error_hook that longjmps out keeps the host process alive.

Defaults are conservative: glp_init_smcp selects the primal simplex with presolve off and msg_lev GLP_MSG_ALL (terminal output). Switch to GLP_DUALP and enable presolve before comparing speed, and note that the benchmark tables do not say which settings they used.

GLPK 5.0 replaced the QMD ordering routines (misc/qmd.c) and glp_gridgen with stubs that call xerror ('temporarily disabled due to licensing problems'), so ord_alg = GLP_ORD_QMD aborts; glp_netgen_prob was removed but left in the Windows .def file (conda-forge patch).

Numbers behind the lp_solve ratio are shifted geometric means in which unsolved instances count at the time limit, and lp_solve solved fewer instances (23 vs GLPK's 31 in October 2019, snippet only), so part of the gap is robustness rather than per-instance speed.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Among catalogued siblings, SCS (first-order conic, no basic solution) and the QP solvers PIQP, QPALM and ProxQP solve continuous problems only; pick GLPK when you need simplex basic solutions, integer variables or MathProg models in a small C library. For pure LP speed, look at HiGHS or Clp, which are not catalogued yet.
verified_claims_summary: HiGHS-team slides (Hall, INFORMS 2019), drawn from Mittelmann's simplex benchmark, give GLPK a relative time of 24-28 against lp_solve's 92-112 (about 3.8-4.3x), and ALGLIB's 90-problem NETLIB run puts GLPK about 2x and lp_solve about 3x behind the leaders (about 1.5x). All of this comes from search snippets: no solver versions, settings, compiler or hardware were seen, and the slides note that HiGHS presolve and crash were off while Clp used its Idiot crash.
status_note: GPL-3.0-or-later; GLPK 5.0 (16 Dec 2020) is still what Homebrew, conda-forge, msys2 and Julia Yggdrasil package in 2026, with no public repository and a GCC 15 build patch needed downstream. The evidence is snippet-only and stale: Mittelmann's LP benchmarks have not included GLPK since at least the December 2022 snapshot in the mittelmann-plots archive.
